text:
I'm in the same situation. Started looking into building high-end-ish PC from scratch for games and fun, and I can tell you that it looks not really good right now in September 2023. 
If I decided to build it now, it would be i7 13700K on a Z790 chipset with DDR5 RAM and the rest of the money would be spent on GPU. 
But 14th gen of Intel processors coming in about 6 weeks (the end of October 2023), which is a refresh of 13th gen. So if I waited 2-3 month, I'd be able to build something like i7 14700K+mobo with Z790 chipset+DDR5 RAM and some kind of a GPU. 
BUT... 5000 series of nvidia GPUS is rumored to be announced in late 2024. As well as 15th gen of intel CPUs is coming in fall 2024, which will have (according to rumors) a new architecture and so on and so forth.   
Granted, 'announced' doesn't mean I'd be able to buy, lets say, 5090 right away, it will probably take a month or two or even 3 minimum (and realistically even more than that) after the announcement for the top-tier cards to hit retail stores. 
It is indeed a hard time for anyone who wants to build a PC from scratch, because if you build it now or 2-3 month from now, you could miss on something that the new generations of hardware will offer in a year. And if you wait a year or year and a half, you could end up in a situation where the prices are even bigger nightmare than they are today, because the AI boom could create new shortages in GPUs and drive the prices even higher.
I'm a little bit all over the place in this comment, but that's my honest illustration of what's going on in the hardware market right now.
